To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of SERS substrates is dependent on the size, shape, and orientation of metal nanoparticles and the density of nanoparticles in the surface array.

(i) the SERS activity of substrates is highly sensitive to the density of nanoparticles on the substrate and (ii) SERS activity is also strongly dependent on the morphology of nanoparticles on the substrates.

the SERS enhancement is a function of the number of hot spots per unit area, and that the hot spots per unit surface area can be increased by using smaller particles and/or by increasing the density of particles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a rational design for the fabrication of nanoscale substrates with improved performance in SERS.
the fabrication of SERS-active substrates by EBL and their characterization by Raman spectroscopy.
the development of new SERS-active substrates for the rapid detection of trace analytes and the use of these substrates to develop new analytical methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SERS signal intensity is strongly dependent on the density of the metal nanoparticles, and that the shape of the metal nanoparticles plays a secondary role in determining the magnitude of the SERS signal.

, for the excitation wavelength employed, SERS enhancement factors are maximized when nanoparticle density is high and the nanoparticle size is small, and when the nanoparticle primary axis is oriented perpendicular to the excitation laser polarization.
the best SERS substrates are those that have the highest density of the smallest metal nanoparticles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a given excitation wavelength, the SERS enhancement is a function of the number of loci, the size and geometry of the loci, and the density of loci on the surface.
the most efficient substrates were those that maximized the density of nanoparticles on the substrate surface.
the SERS signal is strongly dependent on the nanoparticle density of the substrate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SERS signal can be significantly enhanced by increasing the number of metal nanoparticles in the focal volume.
EBL can be used to rapidly and systematically fabricate substrates that are highly sensitive for SERS and that can be tailored to the excitation wavelength of the Raman spectrometer.
the EBL fabrication method is capable of producing substrates that are both highly reproducible and analytically sensitive.
